construction_markdown:
Let `p(U)=U^16+U^5+U^3+U^2+1`, let `F=F_2[U]/(p)`, and write `θ=U mod p`. Every `z∈F` has unique coordinates `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15} z_i θ^i`.

Use the 32,768-point evaluation set

`A={Σ_{i=0}^{14} a_i θ^i : a_i∈F_2}`.

For `z∈F`, define its binary affine encoding

`H(z)=(z_15+Σ_{i=0}^{14} z_i y_i)_{y∈F_2^15}`.

Thus `H` is an explicit linear bijection from `F` to `RM(1,15)`, with parameters `[32768,16,16384]_2`.

For each polynomial `f∈F[X]` of degree at most 64, define

`c_f=(H(f(a)))_{a∈A}`.

Order field coefficients, points of `A`, and inner positions by their increasing binary indices. Set `C={c_f:deg(f)≤64}`. This is the concatenation of a shortened Reed–Solomon code `[32768,65,32704]_{2^16}` with `RM(1,15)`. No padding, shortening after concatenation, or random choice occurs.

For nonzero z∈F, H(z) has weight 16,384 unless z=θ^15, in which case it is the all-one word of weight 32,768.
Thus every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least 32,704·16,384=(2^15-2^6)2^14=2^29-2^20=535,822,336.

The polynomial basis, 32,768 evaluation points, 32,768 inner positions, and both coordinate orderings are specified by binary indices.
The message space is exactly the 65 unrestricted coefficients of a degree-at-most-64 polynomial over F.

proof_markdown:
# Shortened Reed–Solomon code with affine binary inner code

## Theorem

There is a symbolically deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters

`[1,073,741,824, 1,040, 535,822,336]_2`.

Its rate is `1040/2^30=65/2^26`.

## Field certificate

Let `p(U)=U^16+U^5+U^3+U^2+1`. Repeated squaring modulo `p` gives

`U^256 ≡ U^8+U^7+U^3+U` and `U^65536 ≡ U`.

Put `h=U^8+U^7+U^3`, the residue of `U^256+U`. Direct Euclidean division gives

`p=(U^8+U^7+U^6+U^5+U^4+U^2+1)h+(U^2+1)`,

`h=(U^6+U^5+U^4+U^3+U^2+1)(U^2+1)+1`.

Thus `gcd(p,U^256+U)=1`, while `p` divides `U^65536+U`. Every irreducible factor of `p` consequently has degree dividing 16, but none has degree dividing 8. Since the only divisor of 16 not dividing 8 is 16 and `deg p=16`, the polynomial `p` is irreducible. Hence `F=F_2[U]/(p)` is the stated field.

## Construction and binary linearity

Write `θ=U mod p` and represent every `z∈F` uniquely as `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_iθ^i`. Let

`A=span_{F_2}{1,θ,…,θ^14}`.

For `z∈F`, define

`H(z)_y=z_15+Σ_{i=0}^{14}z_i y_i`, for `y∈F_2^15`.

Coefficient extraction and affine evaluation are binary linear. Moreover, `H(z)=0` implies first `z_15=0` by taking `y=0`, and then every `z_i=0` by taking the unit vectors. Thus `H` is injective.

For `f∈F[X]` with `deg f≤64`, concatenate the blocks `H(f(a))`, one for every `a∈A`. Evaluation, coefficient extraction, and `H` are binary linear, so their image `C` is binary linear.

## Exact length and dimension

There are `|A|=2^15` outer blocks and each block has `2^15` coordinates. Therefore

`n=2^15·2^15=2^30=1,073,741,824`.

The polynomial message space has dimension 65 over `F`, hence binary dimension `65·16=1040`. Its encoder is injective: if every binary block vanishes, injectivity of `H` gives `f(a)=0` for every `a∈A`. A nonzero polynomial of degree at most 64 cannot have 32,768 distinct roots, so `f=0`. Therefore `dim_F2(C)=1040`.

## Minimum-distance lower bound

Let `f` be nonzero. It has at most 64 roots in `A`; hence at least `32768-64=32704` blocks contain nonzero symbols.

If `z∈F` is nonzero and some coefficient among `z_0,…,z_14` is nonzero, `H(z)` is a nonconstant affine truth table and has exactly `2^14` ones. If all those coefficients vanish, then `z=θ^15` and `H(z)` is the all-one word of weight `2^15`. Every nonzero block therefore has weight at least `2^14`, and

`wt(c_f)≥32704·2^14=(2^15-2^6)2^14=2^29-2^20=535,822,336`.

This covers every nonzero codeword.

## Attainment

Let `B=span_{F_2}{1,θ,…,θ^5}⊂A`, so `|B|=64`, and put

`f_0(X)=∏_{b∈B}(X-b)`.

For `a∈A\B`, `f_0(a)≠0`. The forbidden set

`S={θ^15/f_0(a):a∈A\B}`

has at most 32,704 elements, strictly fewer than the 65,535 elements of `F*`. Choose the nonzero scalar `λ` of least binary index outside `S`. Then `λf_0` vanishes exactly on `B`, while every other value is nonzero and different from `θ^15`. Its 64 zero blocks have weight zero and its remaining 32,704 blocks each have weight exactly `2^14`. Consequently

`wt(c_{λf_0})=32704·2^14=535,822,336`.

The lower bound is attained, so this is the exact minimum distance. Every choice is finite and deterministic. The candidate should remain under review until independently accepted.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed Frobenius congruences and Euclidean identities force every irreducible factor of p to have degree 16; since p itself has degree 16, it is irreducible.
proof_steps.statement: The specified quotient is the field F_(2^16).

proof_steps.proof: Coefficient extraction followed by affine truth-table evaluation is injective and binary linear; nonconstant affine words are balanced and θ^15 gives the all-one word.
Evaluation of degree-at-most-64 polynomials at 32,768 distinct points is injective; the root bound gives distance at least 32,704, and a polynomial with 64 prescribed roots shows equality.
proof_steps.statement: The outer code has exact parameters [32768,65,32704] over F_(2^16).

proof_steps.proof: Concatenation gives 32,768 blocks of length 32,768, and injectivity gives binary dimension 16·65.
proof_steps.statement: C is binary linear of length 2^30 and dimension 1040.

proof_steps.proof: At least 32,704 blocks are nonzero and every such block weighs at least 16,384.
proof_steps.statement: Every nonzero word has weight at least 535,822,336.

proof_steps.proof: The deterministic scaled polynomial with root set B has 32,704 nonzero values, all avoiding the unique full-weight inner symbol, so every surviving block has weight exactly 16,384.
The target requires outer block distance 32,704 when only inner minimum weight is used; Singleton gives at most (2^16)^65 outer words.
